summary: A steel tower moved to Allen Peak in San Mateo County in 1966, replacing a 1941 CCC-era wooden lookout; closed in 1981 per the register, still standing.

facts.design: Open steel X-braced tower, 22 ft 7 in square at the base, with a 225 sq ft metal-frame cab and pyramidal hip roof (register text gives the height as 51 ft 6 in)

access.note: No public visitor information was found in the sources read. The register says the tower closed in 1981; a 1966 caption places it one mile west of Skyline Boulevard on West Bear Gulch Road. Do not climb.

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry & Fire Protection

events.note: Wooden lookout built on Allen Peak by men from the Gilroy CCC camp, per an August 15, 1941 San Mateo newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts; the register says the 1966 tower replaced a 1941 wooden lookout
County Allen lookout tower reactivated during unseasonably dry weather (November 29, 1956 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Register says the tower was originally an air traffic control tower at Salinas Army Air Base and was moved to this location in 1966 by inmate labor
New steel tower erected to replace the old wooden structure (January 1966 photo caption); register dates the build to 1966
Register says the tower was closed in 1981
Registered November 27, 2016 as US 1147, CA 112; nominated by Scott McClintock

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 37.384386, -122.289853; the Forest Fire Lookout Association list gives 37.38709, -122.29501, about half a kilometer to the northwest. I kept both in the notes and used neither as a correction.

The 1941 newspaper item puts the tower a mile north of the Skyline and La Honda intersection; the 1966 caption puts it one mile west of Skyline Boulevard on West Bear Gulch Road. These may describe the same knoll, but the sources do not say so.

The register says the steel tower came from Salinas Army Air Base. The 1966 caption describes a new steel tower replacing the wooden one but does not say where it came from. Not contradicted, but only the register supports the Salinas origin.

notes_for_editor: Brief's record checks out on 1966 build, NHLR US 1147 / CA 112, San Mateo County, and standing status (FLA). Brief's 'They share a register number' conflict: Wood Butte, Oregon is listed in the FFLOS register as US 1147 (OR 495) in data/towers/or/us-or-wood-butte.json, while Allen is NHLR US 1147 (CA 112). These are different registers, so the numbers may just coincide; I did not verify this against a single register. Brief's coordinates (37.38709, -122.29501) match the FFLA list, not the NHLR point. Register text gives the tower height as '51" 6" high', which is probably 51 ft 6 in; I did not add height_m because the reading is uncertain. Register says it was closed in 1981, which I recorded as staffing 'unstaffed' as of 1981; the register does not use the word 'staffed'. Access is unknown; the register is silent on visiting. Register photos are credited to Scott McClintock; no image URL was captured, so no photos were added. The register's Salinas origin is not confirmed by the other sources read. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story's 'dry spell' wording was replaced with the source's 'unseasonably dry weather', and the 1956 item is now footnoted in the story.
